answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making influence earned, not minted: a new identity starts weightless and gains standing only when established peers countersign its useful work across several epochs. To forge a crowd, an attacker must do real, checked work for each fake or bribe peers who risk their own standing if the fake misbehaves. A whisper of collusion is not enough; like ferrous metal, trust hardens only after repeated heating and testing, so multiplying names multiplies cost, not power.
